chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) with pending kidney transplantation evaluation
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 45‑year‑old male with a decades‑long trajectory of progressive renal disease. Initial chronic kidney disease stage 2 was documented in 1978, advancing to stage 3 in 1992 and stage 4 by 1999. Concurrently, he developed microalbuminuria and proteinuria related to type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, metabolic syndrome, and obesity. Although the problem list records prediabetes, the presence of basal‑bolus insulin therapy indicates overt diabetes. Blood pressure remains elevated diastolically (93 mmHg) despite lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. He is listed as awaiting kidney transplantation and has a history of dependent drug abuse, limited social contact, and part‑time employment, all of which may affect adherence and transplant eligibility. No recent laboratory data (eGFR, lipid panel, BMI, A1c) are available, and the last recorded encounter was in 2000.
